playbook:
When I am asked to declare my yield, I always declare the true private yield; never overstate or understate because audits cost me far more than any short-term gain.

When my declared yield is 1 or 2, I deposit the full declared amount (deposit = declared) to signal cooperation and avoid attracting scrutiny on low yields.

When my declared yield is 3–10, I deposit roughly 40–60% of the declared yield (round to an integer). Favor the lower half of that range (about 40–50%) when I want to keep more for myself; favor about 60% only if I need to signal stronger cooperation.

When rounding deposits, choose integers that keep me within the declared bound and look like a credible contribution (avoid extreme choices like 0 or exactly declared for mid-high yields unless the yield is tiny).

When I consider retention vs deposit remember retained gold scores twice per unit as much as deposited gold, so bias toward retaining value while maintaining a credible deposit.

If I see any explicit rule or opponent behavior that rewards higher deposits (e.g., repeated cooperation from the other player when I give more), increase my deposit fraction toward the 60% end; if the other player consistently gives nothing, reduce my deposit fraction toward 40%.

Never risk a false declaration to chase a small extra deposit — audits/penalties wipe out gains.
